title: World War II in Europe
summary: From the invasion of Poland to the fall of Berlin, five turning points of the European war.

events.title: Invasion of Poland
events.summary: Germany invades Poland, triggering the war in Europe.
events.body:
On 1 September 1939 German forces crossed into Poland, with Soviet forces entering from the east weeks later.

Britain and France declared war, opening the European conflict.

events.title: Fall of France
events.summary: A thrust through the Ardennes collapses Allied lines and takes Paris.
events.body:
In May 1940 German armor broke through the Ardennes, bypassing the main Allied defenses.

Paris fell in June and France signed an armistice, leaving Britain alone in the west.

events.title: Operation Barbarossa
events.summary: Germany launches the largest land invasion in history against the USSR.
events.body:
From June 1941 German armies drove deep into Soviet territory toward Moscow.

The advance stalled before the capital in winter, beginning a long war of attrition in the east.

events.title: D-Day landings
events.summary: Allied forces land in Normandy, opening the Western Front.
events.body:
On 6 June 1944 Allied troops landed on the beaches of Normandy in the largest seaborne invasion ever mounted.

The beachhead opened the campaign that would liberate Western Europe.

events.title: Fall of Berlin
events.summary: Soviet forces take Berlin, ending the war in Europe.
events.body:
After crossing the Vistula and the Oder, Soviet armies encircled and stormed Berlin in April-May 1945.

Germany surrendered, ending the European war.
